dedupe_keys.name: integrated master plan for coastal safety in flanders climate adapt case study

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes the Integrated Master Plan for Coastal Safety that the Flemish Government adopted in 2011 to protect the Flemish coast against storms with a 1-in-1,000-year return period, now and with 30 cm of sea level rise by 2050. It combines green measures (beach and dune nourishment) with grey ones (storm walls, wider seawalls with wave basins and a storm surge barrier), after an emergency programme of critical works in 2004 to 2010. The investment is about 300 million euros, with beach maintenance of about 8 million euros a year; by early 2020 two thirds of the budget was spent or tendered. Coverage is the Flemish coast in West Flanders. The page is accessible online as free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal, published in 2020 and updated in 2026. Caveats: the architectural costs borne by municipalities are left out, and the successor Kustvisie project (2017) will set measures after 2050. Simulation uses: design standards, measures and costs for coastal flood defence and sea level rise adaptation. Related records: the Dutch primary flood defences (data-netherlands-primary-flood-defences-nbpw).
name: Integrated Master Plan for Coastal Safety in Flanders (Climate-ADAPT case study)
outcomes: By early 2020 two thirds of the budget of about 300 million euros was spent or tendered; evaluations reported improved safety.
